Kaaviokuva kahdessa osassa, ei mittakaav: Diagram in two parts, not to scale. In both, a horizontal printed beam sticks out from a wall on the left, and a red force F acts downward on the beam's free end. Thin lines show the print layers. On the left the beam was printed lying down, so the layers run along the beam: this is the strong orientation. On the right the beam was printed standing up, so the layers are across the beam, and next to the wall a crack has opened between two layers: this is the weak orientation.
Kolme leikkauskuvaa vierekkäin, ei mitta: Three cross-sections side by side, not to scale. Each has a grey print bed, a nozzle above it and orange cross-sections of printed filament on the bed. On the left the nozzle is too high: the strands are round, with gaps between them, and they barely stick to the bed. In the middle the nozzle is at the right height: the strands are slightly flattened and touch each other, and the surface is even. On the right the nozzle is too low: the strands are squashed thin, and ridges have squeezed out at their edges.
